articles.headline: TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 roundtables: Go deeper on the challenges founders are solving right now
keyFacts: The TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 will take place at SoWa Power Station in Boston on November 4.
Founders, investors, and experts will host six roundtables covering enterprise AI, vertical strategies, and category building.
TechCrunch is offering a 25 percent ticket discount alongside a buy-one-get-one-free deal.
body: TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 is coming to SoWa Power Station in Boston on November 4, bringing founders, investors, and operators together for a full day of candid conversations, practical sessions, live pitching, networking, and smaller roundtables built for deeper discussion.

The roundtables are where attendees can get especially specific. Bring your questions, share what you are seeing in your own company, and join experts and fellow founders tackling many of the same challenges, from enterprise sales and vertical strategy to AI, lean teams, and building a category that does not exist yet.
Save 25% on your ticket today, and bring a colleague along for free with our limited BOGO deal.
Six roundtables to look forward to at Founder Summit
How to Build Events Strategy Before You Can Afford a Full-Time Events Team
10:45 a.m. – 11:15 a.m. | Roundtable 2

Alexandra Ames, founder and chief event strategist at Blueprint Lab, looks at how early-stage companies can use events strategically before they have the budget or headcount for a dedicated events team. Expect a practical conversation about choosing the right opportunities, defining what success looks like, and making limited resources work harder.
Your First Vertical, and It Happens to Be the Hardest One
11:30 a.m. – 12:00 p.m. | Roundtable 1

Chirag Shah, partner at Define Ventures, explores what happens when the market with the biggest potential is also one of the hardest to enter. Founders navigating regulated industries, complex buyers, or specialized customers can compare notes on making that first major vertical bet.
GraphRAG in Action: Stop Hallucinations with Knowledge Graphs
11:30 a.m. – 12:00 p.m. | Roundtable 2

Shishir Tewari, head of enterprise data engineering at Procore Technologies, gets into one of enterprise AI’s most persistent challenges: trust. The discussion will examine how knowledge graphs and GraphRAG can give AI systems stronger context and help founders build products that work more reliably in real-world organizations.
The Enterprise AI Playbook: How to Close L’Oreal and Vodafone Before You Raise a Series A
1:15 p.m. – 1:45 p.m. | Roundtable 2

Merve Kitapci, managing partner and CGO of ADIN.AI, breaks down what it takes to win major enterprise customers early. From long buying cycles and multiple stakeholders to the credibility that comes with landing the right logo, this is a tactical conversation for founders selling into large organizations before they have a large sales team behind them.
Build Something We Don’t Have a Word for Yet
1:55 p.m. – 2:25 p.m. | Roundtable 2

Andy Tang, partner at Draper Associates, leads a conversation for founders building something that does not fit neatly into an existing category. How do you explain it, sell it, and get investors to understand the opportunity when the market still needs vocabulary for what you are creating?
Small but Mighty: How AI Lets Lean Teams Outship the Giants
2:35 p.m. – 3:05 p.m. | Roundtable 1

Linden Tibbets, CEO and founder of IFTTT, explores how smaller teams can use AI to increase their speed and output without simply adding headcount. For founders thinking about hiring, efficiency, and how to structure an AI-enabled company, the discussion gets directly into what lean teams may be able to do differently now.
Roundtables are where the agenda becomes a conversation

The value of these sessions is not just hearing how someone else approached a problem. It is the chance to ask the question that matters to your company, compare experiences with the people around the table, and leave with ideas you can put to work.

And the roundtables are only one part of the day. Across the Build and Impact Stages, Founder Summit will also tackle product-market fit, hiring, founder leadership, fundraising, pitching, and what it takes to build and scale companies outside the Bay Area.

Attendees can hear founder perspectives from leaders, such as Toast co-founder Steve Fredette, then see founders put their stories to the test during the live “So You Think You Can Pitch?” competition. articles.headline: Which G6 teams could benefit most from James Madison's loss in race for CFP berth?
keyFacts: James Madison lost to Appalachian State 34-31 on Thursday night, which likely eliminated the team from the race for the lone Group of Six playoff berth.
Boise State and Oregon State from the Pac-12 are among the schools best positioned to benefit from James Madison's loss.
New Mexico, North Dakota State, Air Force, and UTSA are also mentioned as teams that could contend for the playoff spot if they win out.
body: James Madison's loss to Appalachian State on Thursday night was the latest domino to fall in the race for the lone Group of Six spot in the College Football Playoff.
The berth goes to the highest-ranked team from the American, Conference USA, MAC, Mountain West, Pac-12 or Sun Belt conferences in the final College Football Playoff selection committee rankings.

The first committee rankings don't come out until Nov. 3, but they typically follow the polls closely, so it's a safe bet that James Madison was a top contender before its 34-31 loss. The Dukes were just outside the Associated Press Top 25 this week and were second in votes among G6 schools.

Because the G6 includes 70 teams competing for one bid, any loss is major -- especially against other G6 schools. That means James Madison, a member of the Sun Belt Conference, likely is out of the race.

Appalachian State (5-2) might have capitalized on its big win, but the Mountaineers already had losses to North Carolina State and Old Dominion. The Old Dominion loss is a killer -- the Monarchs are just 2-5.
Here are the schools best positioned to benefit most from likely having James Madison out of the way:
Boise State and Oregon State, Pac-12
Boise State (6-1) opened the season with a 34-27 loss at Oregon, but the Broncos have won five straight and are currently the highest-ranked G6 team at No. 21 in the Associated Press Top 25.
The Broncos also have star power -- Dylan Riley is second in the FBS with 166.3 yards rushing per game.

Boise State's wins over Western Michigan and Memphis have held up well. Western Michigan, which nearly beat Michigan in its opener, was the MAC's best hope before its 32-7 loss to Boise State weeks later likely ended its bid. Memphis is clearly a talented team, but the Tigers (6-2) had a killer loss to Tulane last week.
Boise State RB Dylan Riley leads the FBS with 835 rushing yards.
— Underdog CFB (@UnderdogCFB) October 13, 2026

Boise State's biggest regular-season challenge remaining appears to be a home game against Oregon State on Nov. 14. The Beavers feature one of the most productive offenses in college football and a Heisman contender in freshman receiver Jesse Legree, who leads the nation in yards receiving and receiving touchdowns.
Should Boise State win out, the Broncos would have a strong chance of getting the bid.

Oregon State (5-2) might have a case if it wins out. The Beavers' only two losses are at No. 14 Houston and at home against No. 8 Texas Tech. They have won five straight while averaging 51 points per game during the streak.
Oregon State was fourth among G6 teams with three votes in this week's AP poll.
New Mexico, North Dakota State and Air Force, Mountain West
New Mexico (5-1) appears to have a shot if things fall the right way. They have a loss, but it was 14-6 at Oklahoma. The Lobos were third among G6 schools in AP votes this week, with six.

New Mexico leads the nation in scoring defense. The Lobos face North Dakota State (6-1), which ranks nationally second in scoring defense, on Saturday. This game would have been even bigger had North Dakota State not lost to UNLV on Oct. 10.
New Mexico plays UNLV on Nov. 14 and Air Force (5-1) on Nov. 28. Wins there could put the Lobos in prime position to make the committee think.
North Dakota State and Air Force could make a case if they beat New Mexico, barring losses in other games.
UTSA, American

The Roadrunners (6-1) have won four straight, and their only loss was a 30-6 setback to Texas. They don't have a big-name opponent the rest of the way, so they'll probably need to win out and get some help to be strongly considered.

articles.headline: 8 New TV Shows to Watch This Weekend on Netflix, HBO, and Hulu (October 23-25)
keyFacts: Polygon published a list of eight television shows available to watch on streaming platforms like Netflix, HBO, and Hulu for the weekend.
The recommendations include returning second seasons for Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and The Terminal List, alongside new episodes of Nobody Wants This.
Other highlighted releases feature the Canadian thriller series Yaga on AMC+, the fourth season of Lupin, and the complete series of Orphan Black on HBO Max.
body: Happy weekend! It’s a slow week for TV releases. Over the past month, shows like Carrie, Crystal Lake, and VisionQuest dropped, keeping many viewers busy. But things are picking up soon. In the coming months, we’ll have the return of the final season of Yellowjackets, the third season of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, and more.

In the meantime, we have some shows to recommend. Cyberpunk: Edgerunners is back with its second season, bringing viewers back to Night City, which looks just as incredible as it did the first time around. The romantic comedy Nobody Wants This continues to explore the romance between Joanne and Noah, who’ve just moved in together.

There are also various offerings for genre fans. Yaga, a Canadian series starring Heated Rivalry’s overnight star Hudson Williams, is inspired by the legend of Baba Yaga (but is unrelated to John Wick). Lupin returns with its fourth season, continuing the story of a charismatic con artist. Orphan Black is streaming in full on HBO Max, making it the perfect opportunity for it to reach a wider audience.
Other noteworthy shows include Phony, a comedy-mystery following a mother and son with a co-dependent relationship, and the second season of Chris Pratt’s The Terminal List. Happy watching.
1 Cyberpunk: Edgerunners
- Available on Netflix
- Genre: Anime
- Episode count: 10
- Cast: Kentaro Tone, Koki Uchiyama, Momoka Terasawa

Set in the world of the Cyberpunk 2077 video game, Edgerunners is back with a second season, following a whole new cast of characters whose lives intersect in Night City. Some of this season’s storylines include an edgerunner past his prime on a path to redemption, a teenager who wants to rebel from her Corpo family, and a cinephile trying to preserve traditional movie-making in a world where the art form has become obsolete.
Per our Polygon review:

Across 10 episodes, director Kai Ikarashi and the teams at CD Projekt Red and Studio Trigger deliver another spectacular collision of corporate cruelty, dangerous technology, and people pushing themselves past their limits. The ingredients are familiar, sometimes a little too much. But an extraordinary ensemble and the relationships that develop among its members make this return to Night City richer, more rewarding, and downright better.
2 Nobody Wants This
- Available on Netflix
- Genre: Romance
- Episode count: 10
- Cast: Kristen Bell, Adam Brody, Justine Lupe

Nobody Wants This has become one of Netflix’s biggest recent hits, capitalizing on Millennials’ nostalgia from two of their great teen icons: Kristen Bell and Adam Brody. The pair play Joanne, a sex podcaster, and Noah, a rabbi, who fall in love despite their different backgrounds and interests. The third season finds their relationship in its most serious moment yet, with the two moving in and Joanne considering converting to Judaism.
3 Yaga
- Available on AMC+
- Genre: Thriller
- Episode count: 8
- Cast: Hudson Williams, Carrie-Anne Moss, Noah Reid

Yaga is based on a stage play, which is, in turn, based on the Slavic myth of Baba Yaga. The series begins with a detective (Noah Reid) investigating the disappearance of Henry Park (Hudson Williams), the heir to a powerful fishery. The investigation leads to an encounter with a university professor (Carrie-Anne Moss) with an interest in younger men.
4 Lupin
- Available on Netflix
- Genre: Crime
- Episode count: 8
- Cast: Omar Sy, Ludivine Sagnier, Shirine Boutella

Lupin is back with a fourth season. The hit Netflix series follows Assane Diop, a con artist who draws inspiration for his crimes from the fictional character and master of disguise Arsène Lupin. The season picks up four years after season three, with Diop newly released from prison, ready to leave his life of crime behind.
5 The Terminal List
- Available on Prime Video
- Genre: Action
- Episode count: 8
- Cast: Chris Pratt, Constance Wu, Jared Shaw

Chris Pratt is back with more action in The Terminal List, which follows James Reece, a Navy SEAL who was ambushed on a mission in Afghanistan and got his revenge on those who were guilty. The second season drags Reece into an even larger conspiracy, taking him to different parts of the world, this time as a CIA operative.
6 Phony
- Available on Hulu
- Genre: Comedy-mystery
- Episode count: 8
- Cast: Sam Nivola, Connie Britton, Mahaela Park

Phony follows high school student Sonny (Sam Nivola) and his mom, Ellen (Connie Britton), who have an unusually close relationship. After a car crash, Sonny wakes up from a coma and grows convinced that his mother has been replaced by an identical impostor, with no one believing him.
7 Newlyweds
- Available on Peacock
- Genre: Comedy
- Episode count: 13
- Cast: Tea Leoni, Tim Daly, Jamie Lee Curtis

Newlyweds sounds like a show from a different era, following a newly married couple, made up of a free-spirited woman and a buttoned-up guy, and how they balance their relationship and contrasting personalities. The show is a sitcom, with each episode recorded in front of a live audience.
8 Orphan Black
- Available on HBO Max
- Genre: Sci-fi
- Episode count: 50 episodes total
- Cast: Tatiana Maslany, Jordan Gavaris, Evelyne Brochu

Orphan Black is now on HBO Max, introducing the series to a wider audience. Led by Tatiana Maslany, the series follows Sarah Manning, an ex-con who returns home to reunite with her family, including her daughter, her adoptive brother, and adoptive mother. Sarah's plans for a peaceful life are quickly disrupted when she witnesses a woman jumping onto the train tracks. As if that wasn’t horrifying enough, the woman looks just like her.
Per our Polygon recommendation:

Underneath a complicated conspiracy plot that involves scary corporations, mad scientists, awful tests on human subjects, and dozens of clones, the series features one of the best performances of all time. Through her years in the show, Tatiana Maslany went from an unknown Canadian actress to an Emmy winner, playing 17 distinct clones across five seasons. More than a decade later, while some of the series’ special effects have aged, the scenes of Maslany’s clones speaking, yelling, hugging, and dancing with each other feel as magical and unique as they did when they first aired, luring you into believing that there really are multiple women onscreen.

articles.headline: Ex-49ers kicker Robbie Gould leaves Illinois high school coaching job
keyFacts: Former NFL kicker Robbie Gould resigned as the head football coach at St. Viator High School after two seasons.
According to school President Ryan Aiello, Gould stepped down to spend more time with his family after compiling an 8-20 record over three total high school coaching seasons.
Gould played the final six seasons of his 18-year NFL career with the San Francisco 49ers.
body: FILE: Kicker Robbie Gould of the San Francisco 49ers looks on from the sidelines against the Los Angeles Rams in the fourth quarter at Levi's Stadium on Oct. 3, 2022, in Santa Clara, Calif. (Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images)
As the 49ers suffer through Eddie Piñeiro's worst stretch as a kicker since he joined San Francisco last year, the most reliable kicker in 49ers history has left his high school coaching job.

This week, former San Francisco 49ers kicker Robbie Gould resigned from the head coaching role at St. Viator High School, according to multiple reports . Gould spent two seasons at the private school in Arlington Heights, a suburb approximately 20 miles northwest of Chicago.

Gould, 43, started his high school head coaching career at Rolling Meadows in 2024, going 5-5 that season and making the playoffs. But he left that school after a single season to head to St. Viator, saying in a press conference that the private school was "No. 1 on my list" of schools he could see himself coaching at while his pre-teen children grew up and potentially played for him.

But on the field , St. Viator struggled to a 1-8 record in 2025 and a 2-7 record in 2026. Now, Gould has decided to step down. According to a statement distributed to the media by school President Ryan Aiello, Gould made the decision so he could spend more time with his family. In three seasons, Gould's overall coaching record is 8-20.

Gould spent the final six seasons of his 18-year NFL career with the 49ers. He made 87.5% of his field goals while with San Francisco, peaking with a 33-for-34 season in 2018. His range slowly dwindled over the years, with his longest made kick in 2022, his final season, being from 51 yards out. But Gould was always excellent on extra points, making 96.1% of point-after tries in his six Niner seasons and never missing more than two in a single season (and that was with the longer extra point the entire time, too).

Overall, Gould is second in 49ers history in field goals made (161) and third in field goal percentage among kickers with more than a season's worth of games (87.5%). He also was perfect on all 40 of his kicks in the playoffs for the 49ers. It's a pretty easy call to say Gould was the most reliable kicker the 49ers have ever had.

This year, Piñeiro has already missed three extra points in six weeks - two in Week 3 against the Cardinals and one last week against the Commanders. He's also missed three of his nine field goals attempts on the year.

The Niners signed Piñeiro after a disastrous performance from Jake Moody in Week 1 last year, leading the team to cut the player they chose in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft to replace Gould. That pick, intended to improve the team's field goal range, turned out to be disastrous over time and led to the sudden dismissal after one game last season.

Piñeiro came in and solidified the position , only missing one field goal all season and making a career-long 59-yarder to help beat the Rams . The 49ers rewarded him with a four-year, $17 million contract with $10 million guaranteed. But Piñeiro did miss five extra points in his 16 total games (regular season and playoffs) and now Piñeiro is missing both at an alarming rate.

As the 49ers get closer to a likely playoff run, the spotlight on the kicking game will only get brighter, especially if there are more struggles. Of course, it's been four seasons since Gould last kicked in an NFL game, so who knows if he's even continued to practice the craft. But you can't be better than "perfect in the playoffs" like Gould was in red and gold, and that's something that will surely be on the minds of the Niners fans and leadership as the season churns along.

articles.headline: F1 star Charles Leclerc makes BBQ stop at Austin's Terry Black's
keyFacts: Scuderia Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc visited Terry Black's Barbecue in Austin, Texas, ahead of the F1 United States Grand Prix.
Terry Black's Barbecue shared photos on social media of Leclerc posing with staff and pitmasters at the restaurant on Barton Springs Road.
Leclerc is competing in the U.S. Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas alongside other top Formula 1 drivers.
body: F1 Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc poses for a photo in front of Terry Black's BBQ on Barton Springs Road in Austin, Texas. (Marcus Vargas/Courtesy of Terry Black's Barbecue)

A legendary Formula 1 star made a pit stop for a different kind of fueling up at a beloved Central Texas barbecue joint before his next big race. Scuderia Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc dined at Terry Black's Barbecue while in Austin this week for the F1 United States Grand Prix.

The Texas-born BBQ restaurant chain shared photos of Leclerc's visit on Wednesday, October 21 to Terry Black's original Austin location on Barton Springs Road. In the Instagram post, Leclerc posed for a photo in front of the restaurant and another alongside Terry Black's staff and pitmasters.
"Great having Charles Leclerc join us at Terry Black's Austin last night," Terry Black's caption said. "Welcome to Texas F1 fans."

Leclerc is one of several F1 drivers competing in this year's U.S. Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas from Thursday, October 22 to Sunday, October 25. He, alongside his Ferrari teammate, Lewis Hamilton, are recognized as some of the best F1 drivers in the world.
F1 driver Charles Leclerc poses for a photo with Terry Black's BBQ staff in Austin, Texas. (Marcus Vargas/Courtesy of Terry Black's Barbecue)
Leclerc has won nine F1 races for Ferrari since his debut in 2018, while Hamilton has secured a record 106 total Grand Prix wins in his F1 career since 2007 at McLaren, Mercedes and now Ferrari.
Terry Black's Barbecue is one of the most popular BBQ joints in Austin for its famous trays of smoked meats, attracting tourists and celebrities from far and wide.

The fast-growing Austin chain has served dozens of big names over the years at its various Texas locations including Becky G , Justin Timberlake and even another F1 driver, Oscar Piastri of McLaren, last year .

body: A big night of fights is set to go down in Abu Dhabi on Saturday. The is headlined by a pair of title fights, including undefeated Movsar Evloev challenging Alexander Volkanovski for the UFC featherweight championship in the main event.
Evloev holds a perfect 20-0 professional record, but he'll face the biggest test of his career in Volkanovski, who is on his second run as 145-pound champion at age 38.

In the co-main event, Petr Yan and Merab Dvalishvili will clash in a rubber match for the bantamweight championship. Dvalishvili won their first meeting en route to winning the championship and a lengthy title run, but dropped the belt to Yan in their December rematch.

UFC 333 expert picks

With such a massive main event on tap, the crew at CBS Sports went ahead with predictions and picks for the main card from Brian Campbell, Brent Brookhouse, Shakiel Mahjouri, Michael Mormile and Brandon Wise.
Alexander Volkanovski vs. Movsar Evloev predictions

Campbell: Volkanovski's longevity has been remarkable to see, especially after he bounced back from stoppage losses to Islam Makhachev and Ilia Topuria to regain the featherweight title. But it must be said that both of his victories since those damaging defeats came against the all-action but technically limited Diego Lopes, whom Evloev defeated by decision in 2023. For whatever Evloev lacks as a finisher inside the Octagon, he has size, an incredible motor and a physical grappling style that has the potential to wear down the 38-year-old Volkanovski in the championship rounds. He also has a better fight IQ than what Lopes showed against Volkanovski over 10 rounds.

Brookhouse: There are few fights where I will pick against Volkanovski until I've truly seen time catch up to him. Evloev has tremendous wrestling and a willingness to use that wrestling to grind out ugly wins, but Volkanovski has a well-rounded game that also features strong takedown defense. Volkanovski has been here before and he's got the kind of gritty, gutsy game that should require Evloev to do more than just wrestle. While Evloev has shown some strong skills when forced to fight on the feet, Volkanovski has brilliant timing and distance management tools that should let him edge out the fight on the cards.

Mahjouri: Volkanovski says he'll deliver such a sublime performance that fans will think he's de-aged. I'm inclined to believe him. The champion doesn't mean to disrespect his challenger. In fact, he believes Evloev is supremely talented. Volkanovski's confidence stems from the style matchup. He sharpened his grappling defense in preparation for two lightweight fights with Islam Makhachev. On the feet, it's his fight to lose. Volkanovski has a deeper, more nuanced striking arsenal and can fight without fear of being knocked out. Evloev has stopped three opponents by strikes, and none were in the UFC. Evloev is tenacious and will make Volkanovski work early. However, as the fight goes on, expect Volkanovski to break ahead and deliver exactly the performance he predicts.
Petr Yan vs. Merab Dvalishvili predictions

Campbell: After Yan rebounded from a series of losses and injuries, he returned against Dvalishvili a new fighter in their December rematch. Yan took "The Machine" down five times, shut down Dvalishvili's wrestling attack and proved he could match him from the standpoint of pace and cardio. And if Yan can do the same and make their trilogy bout into a kickboxing match, it's hard not to imagine the same scenario from 10 months ago happening again. Dvalishvili was also hurt multiple times in their rematch, including on a pair of body kicks in Round 3 that likely would've finished any other opponent. If Yan can continue to widen the gap between them in terms of striking variety and potency, a stoppage isn't out of the question.

articles.headline: Street Fighter 6 Players Reeling After Capcom Takes Down Popular Community Resource Site
keyFacts: Capcom issued a legal request demanding that the website Ultimate Frame Data remove its Street Fighter 6 section.
The legal letter stated that the site displayed hitbox and collision information not accessible through normal gameplay using unauthorzed mods.
Site operator MetalMusicMan complied with the demand and removed the Street Fighter 6 data.
body: Street Fighter 6 players hoping to study up on their favorite characters ahead of their next tournament appearance are down one more community resource. Ultimate Frame Data, a website where you could study character hitboxes, announced that it would be removing the SF6 portion of the website after receiving a legal request from Capcom.

MetalMusicMan posted the letter that Ultimate Frame Data had received from Capcom’s legal team. “We have confirmed that the page contains hitbox and collision-related information for Street Fighter 6 that is not ordinarily visible or accessible through normal gameplay,” the letter read. “Accordingly, we kindly request that you review the content in question and consider removing or disabling access to the relevant material by October 30, 2026.” MetalMusicMan made the decision to take down the SF6 data, writing on X, “Not my choice, sorry everyone.”
I got a takedown notice from Capcom IP / Legal today. No more Street Fighter 6 on UFD / ultimateframedata.
Not my choice, sorry everyone : pic.twitter.com/dvsJGT6ujR
— Metal (@MetalMusicMan_) October 23, 2026

In fighting games, hitboxes are the defined sections of a character’s body that determine the range and shape of their attacks. Hitboxes are invisible during regular gameplay, but can be made visible through the use of mods. Studying hitboxes can help players improve their performance and there are many hitbox resources available for the myriad games in the fighting game genre. In its letter, Capcom claims that it does not authorize the use of the modding tools necessary to obtain the hitbox data and as such, the data must be taken down.

Naturally, the SF6 community is in disbelief that Capcom, generally considered an FGC-friendly company, would take such an extreme step when Nintendo, a very anti-FGC company, would not. Ultimate Frame Data also hosts hitbox info for Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, which has, so far, remained untouched.

articles.headline: Is the GPU crisis down to real shortages, or is it market manipulation?
keyFacts: Business Insider reported that Amazon is buying more Nvidia AI server racks than its data centers can currently deploy.
Analyst Ed Zitron claimed Nvidia's AI sales strategy is causing severe shortages and price spikes for consumer GeForce gaming GPUs.
Shortages and high prices for graphics cards, RAM, and SSDs are expected to worsen next year.
body: - A new report claims that Amazon is buying up more AI GPU racks than it can deploy in data centers
- An analyst links this report to Nvidia's GeForce GPU supply woes, theorizing that there's a connection
- The contention is that Nvidia is deliberately 'channel stuffing' or in other words, pushing an excess of AI GPUs to the detriment of gaming GPU chips
Nvidia's supply issues with its gaming GPUs are seemingly the result of a strategy to get AI giants to stock up on more graphics chips than they can handle, if fresh reports are to be believed.
You can't have failed to notice the stock issues around Nvidia's GeForce GPUs, and the spike in prices that has happened over the past few months, particularly for higher-end graphics cards.

Well, according to the musings of tech pundit and analyst Ed Zitron (via RespawnFirst) — who picked up on a report by Business Insider — the consumer GPU shortage is a direct result of Nvidia pushing AI graphics cards on the likes of Amazon.

Business Insider informs us that Amazon (or rather AWS) is buying more Nvidia GPUs than it can deploy. Apparently, racks of the AI graphics cards are being kept unused in holding warehouses until there's power available at the data centers where they'll be used (electricity capacity, not space, is the issue here).

Amazon is paying out huge sums for these GB300 racks from Nvidia, and according to an internal email that Business Insider got hold of, a new 'Early Rack Receipt' process (buying these GPUs upfront, before they're installed) saw some $5 billion worth of server racks paid for in August 2026. Seemingly $3 billion more are on order every month for the "foreseeable future" going by another email.
We're told one AWS team didn't have a "clear forecasted path" for getting the purchased racks installed — in other words, they're not even sure when these GPUs might be used.

Zitron's argument is based on a key phrase in the Business Insider report, where the author states that the reason for the switch in policy — Amazon only used to pay for racks when they were installed in a data center — is that "Amazon has to compete more for scarce resources as it jockeys with rivals for access to Nvidia GPUs and other AI components."
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.

The conclusion Zitron draws is that this is basically indicating that Nvidia is making Amazon, and others buying up AI GPUs, compete with each other by agreeing to order a whole pile of them there and then — more than they possibly need — otherwise they won't get their allocation (presumably).
Analysis: GPU misery is clear enough to see

In short, these AI GPUs aren't actually needed as such — not by Amazon in this quantity, as per the Business Insider report — but Nvidia is effectively strong-arming the company into buying the chips, or as Zitron puts it, this is "deliberate channel stuffing." Meaning Nvidia is forcing this AI demand artificially to the seeming detriment of GeForce GPUs, with lesser chip supply for those gaming cards causing price inflation and general misery for gamers.
Obviously we need to take this with a good deal of caution — that goes for the initial report from Business Insider, and doubly so with the theorizing that Zitron applies on top of that article.

There's no denying, however, that we have witnessed a frustrating shortage of consumer GPUs, and in particular Nvidia's high-end gaming graphics cards have become painfully thin on the ground — and pricey. The RTX 5090 is either unobtainable, save through third-party marketplace sellers trying to gouge you out of the best part of 10 grand (in the US), or it's hideously expensive to the tune of over £6,000 in the UK, for example.

What's worse is the RTX 5080 is now getting ridiculously pricey too, reaching £1,400 in the UK. And in the US on Newegg, there's now only one model for sale (direct from the retailer) — and it'll set you back $2,000. It's all getting silly, frankly, and with rumors that the RTX 5090 is being discontinued doing the rounds — speculation Nvidia has denied, I should make clear — it's currently a disappointingly gloomy picture for GPUs.

The expectation is that matters are only going to get worse for RAM, SSDs, and GPUs, as next year rolls into town — and that makes all the above theorizing seem a bit more plausible. It's certainly clear that Nvidia's priority is AI GPUs rather than GeForce graphics cards because of the profits involved with AI, but of course, Team Green is a business — so what do we expect? Prioritization is one thing, though, and the levelled accusation of the practice of 'channel stuffing' is entirely another.

articles.headline: Ipswich v Nottingham Forest: Premier League – live
keyFacts: Williams scored the opening goal for Nottingham Forest in the 13th minute after receiving a pass from Munoz.
Enciso equalized for Ipswich Town in the 41st minute following a mishit backpass by Milenkovic.
The score was tied 1-1 at half-time after a first half that included goals from both teams.
body: Half-time postbag. “There’s always one relegated team per season which is too good to go down. I don’t think it’ll be Forest this season, because they really do look too good to go down, but it could be them if they don’t start putting away their chances. That said, the team too good to go down will probably be Manchester City” – Kári Tulinius.
“Just to underline how early in the season it still is, the live table has had Forest in 18th, 10th and 17th in the space of half an hour” – Dave Estherby
“With a clever Austrian manager, a feisty Austrian midfielder (Xaver Schlager) and a crafty Swiss winger (Dan Ndoye), Forest have got a bit of Alpine sturdiness about them these days” – Peter Oh
45 min: Enciso romps down the right and swings in low. Emersonn can’t reach the ball before Sels, who snaffles. There will be two additional first-half minutes.

43 min: Forest were thinking about a two-goal lead for a few seconds there. But then the ball was turned over, and after one big clanger by Milenkovic, now look! Forest may go all the way back to the Ouattara challenge on Ndoye, but that’s water under the bridge now.
GOAL! Ipswich Town 1-1 Nottingham Forest (Enciso 41)

Cunha leads a four-on-two counter but takes a heavy touch. He’s easily dispossessed, and that allows O’Shea to blooter clear. Milenkovic should deal with the ball on halfway, but his attempt to pass back to his keeper is mishit. Underhit. Seriously so. Enciso tears away with it, reaches the edge of the box, and slots past Sels and into the bottom left!
39 min: An Ipswich free kick in a dangerous position, 25 yards out on the right. But Enciso’s delivery is no good, and it’s an easy clearance for Cunha.

37 min: Gibbs-White tries to release Ndoye down the inside-left channel, but his team-mate is clumsily brought down by Ouattara. The referee waves play on, much to Forest’s annoyance. Was Ouatarra the last man? Probably not, but that should have been a free kick at the very least.

34 min: Walton may have got a little bit on that Gibbs-White bundle, by the way, taking some sting off the ball to make things a bit easier for his team-mate Davis to hack clear. Either way, the Ipswich defence mucked in and got the job done.

32 min: … Diop nearly flashes an own goal past Walton. The ball just clears the crossbar. The second corner of the sequence comes in, and Ndoye, facing the wrong way and not obviously aware of what’s going on, sends an unconventional header, let’s say, wide left.

31 min: Ndoye barrels into acres down the right. He crosses low and long for Gibbs-White, who slides in and guides the ball back across Walton and the face of goal, towards the bottom right. It’s heading in, but Davis hooks off the line just in time, at the expense of a corner, from which …

30 min: Enciso has the ball just to the right of the Forest D. He should release Fatawu into the box with a pass down the inside-right channel, but tries to chop back infield for a shot instead. He’s dispossessed, and the crowd make that sort of noise that most people emit when Ed Sheeran offers to sing.

26 min: Ipswich counter and carve out their first big opportunity of the match. A ball swung in from the left. Emersonn takes his second touch of the game, and it’s nearly worthy of an assist. His far-post header’s cushioned back into the path of Philogene, who simply has to score from 12 yards, but bashes his shot straight at Sels, who parries. Forest clear their lines.
25 min: Gibbs-White drives down the inside-left channel and upon reaching the edge of the box, uses Diop as a shield while power-curling towards the top right. The shot sails inches wide.

23 min: Fatawu advances down the right and looks for Emersonn in the Forest box with a low diagonal. Emersonn can’t get there. He’s only touched the ball once so far, and that to restart the game after the goal.
18 min: Enciso bursts into some space down the middle and draws a foul out of Gibbs-White and McAtee, who clip him to the floor in a scissor attack. Free kick, in a central position, 25 yards out.
17 min: Munoz again makes a nuisance of himself down the right. He feeds Gibbs-White, whose cross is claimed by Walton, but only at the second grab. Forest are getting plenty of joy down this flank.
15 min: Delap played his role in that goal as well, winning the first phase of possession, taking down a long pass that gave Munoz something to work with. An absolute belter in the end.
GOAL! Ipswich Town 0-1 Nottingham Forest (Williams 13)

This is a lovely goal. Munoz fights for possession down the right, bouncing off O’Shea. The ball breaks to Gibbs-White, who immediately sends Munoz scampering further down the wing. Munoz, in space, swings long for the in-rushing Williams, who cuts in from the left and meets the ball first time, sweeping it powerfully past Walton, who has no chance! Lovely move.
9 min: Fatawu cuts in from the right. He’s got Enciso and Emersonn in the middle, but takes on the shot instead, curling viciously towards the top left. But the shot’s always heading high and wide.

8 min: Philogene ships possession carelessly in the centre circle, and suddenly Forest are attacking four on two. Gibbs-White feeds Delap down the inside-right channel; the former Ipswich striker enters the box before slicing a poor shot wide right. Forest looking lively.

7 min: Forest win a free kick out on the right. Gibbs-White curls it long. Ndoye wins a header, cushioning down into the path of Cunha, who from the edge of the box pearls a fierce drive towards the top left. Walton parries well. That’ll have warmed his palms.

5 min: Philogene drives down the middle of the park. He’s heading down a blind alley, but when he loses the ball it fortunately deflects into the path of Enciso, who has a dig from distance. Miles over the bar.
4 min: Munoz hares after a long pass down the right. His cross is calmly dealt with by Diop. Forest first to pretty much everything during these very early exchanges.
2 min: It’s windy in Suffolk. Walton batters a clearance upfield as best he can. Forest very much playing with the wind at their back in this first half.
Most everyone takes the knee … there’s no room for racism … then Forest get the ball rolling. Or flying. Gibbs-White hoicks it straight out for a goal kick.
The teams are out! Ipswich in blue, Forest in red. A fine Friday-evening post-work, pre-match-pints-fuelled atmosphere at Portman Road. We’ll be off in a couple of minutes!

Gary O’Neil talks to Sky. “The team today allows us to get more attacking players on the pitch … we want as many as we can … we need to be really secure with the ball … it will be a test … they are a very direct side … a big test of us … one that we can learn a bit more about ourselves and hopefully come out on top.”

Oliver Glasner speaks to Sky Sports: “When we watch our performances … we feel we could have four, five or six points more … we are doing everything that is necessary to get the win … it is really English weather today! … I expect a very intense game … this is what we have to match … Morgan [Gibbs-White] is maybe the key player in our attack … he is unlucky, he could have five, six, seven assists already … he is very important.”

Nottingham Forest also make two changes to their starting XI, after their 1-0 loss at home to the champions Arsenal. Morgan Gibbs-White and Nikola Milenković replace Ousmane Diomande, who drops to the bench, and Nicolás Domínguez, who misses out altogether.

Ipswich make two changes to their starting XI following their 3-2 defeat at Manchester City last weekend. Abdul Fatawu and Jaden Philogene come in for Jacob Greaves and Daizen Maeda, who drop to the bench.

At last, the 1978 show! That year marking the start of imperial phases for both of these clubs: Ipswich Town won their first and only FA Cup, Nottingham Forest their sole league championship. Within another three years, Town were lifting the Uefa Cup (and really should have won another league title to go with Sir Alf’s heroic flash-in-the-pan) by which point Forest were two-time European champions. A pair of genuinely legendary managers, too, in Bobby Robson and Brian Clough. Glory days colliding, banner moments coinciding. Could it all happen again? Well, there’s no point anyone pulling on their boots if we’re not allowed to dream, so why not? Ipswich can go as high as fifth for the evening, though they’d have to win big, while Forest could catapult themselves into the comfort of mid-table. And after that, a world of possibility stretches out ahead. Bobby and Brian showed us how. Kick-off is at 8pm BST. It’s on!

articles.headline: AOC doubles down on radical transgender activism
keyFacts: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez defended transgender rights at an event, asserting that compromising trans rights compromises every citizen's rights.
Transgender activist groups praised Ocasio-Cortez's remarks, while the author argued her stance harms female-only sports and spaces.
Author Brad Polumbo argued that Ocasio-Cortez's record on transgender issues could damage her potential future presidential ambitions.
body: When Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) recently quipped that “Woke 1 was crazy,” some thought the progressive darling might attempt a more centrist rebrand ahead of 2028 presidential speculation. But Ocasio-Cortez just shattered any illusion that she’s moving away from extreme left-wing ideology with new comments doubling down on the most extreme version of transgender activism.

Here’s what happened. The New York congresswoman was asked about transgender issues at a More Perfect University event Thursday night . A transgender-identifying questioner, a biological male, asked, “Trans people in America feel that we have been abandoned by the Democratic Party, that we are a losing issue, that it’s not worth defending us … what do you say to that?”

“They’re wrong!” Ocasio-Cortez replied. “The moment you compromise the rights of a trans person in America, you compromise the rights of every citizen of America. I support the rights of trans women because I’m a girl’s girl.”
Huh?
Just like that, Ocasio-Cortez incoherently reaffirmed her support for some of the most fringe and controversial ideas in modern American politics.

Of course, people who identify as transgender are entitled to the very same constitutional and legal rights as anyone else, whether that’s their right to free expression, due process, to vote, to own firearms in self-defense, etc. And I have always maintained that, as adults, they should be free to live their personal lives however they wish and modify their bodies however they like. But that’s not what’s at issue here. The contentious questions at the heart of the transgender debate emerge when biology and self-identity conflict; when there are competing rights claims — and, whether Ocasio-Cortez admits it or not, only one side can get their way.
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) campaigns for Michigan Democratic gubernatorial candidate Abdul el Sayed in Detroit, July 28, 2018. (Paul Sancya/AP)

You either have female-only sports separated by biological sex, or, as Ocasio-Cortez has consistently supported, you don’t. That results in absurd and unfair situations like female athletes facing exposure to male genitalia in the locker room, having to physically wrestle biological male opponents, or, most recently, losing out on first place in a cross-country meet to a male athlete who “switched” genders mid-season when he went from 75th place among boys to dominating the girls. What part of supporting that insanity is consistent with being a “girl’s girl”?

And the sports issue is just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the many ways in which extreme transgender activism undercuts a genuine understanding of women’s rights. Transgender activist groups, which are already lauding Ocasio-Cortez’s newest comments , have fought successfully to get biological males who self-identify as women placed in women’s prisons in “progressive” states like California — even sex offenders! In some cases, these transgender-identifying inmates are accused of sexually assaulting female inmates they gain access to under these insane policies. Is supporting that what makes Ocasio-Cortez a “girl’s girl”?

Then, of course, there’s the debate over whether female-only spaces are allowed to exist, or whether they must be open to some biological males. This results in absurd situations like Washington state forcing a Korean spa — where women bathe nude — to admit male patrons with penises. (You know, just girly things!)
SUPREME COURT DECLINES TO LET TRUMP END TRANSGENDER SURGERIES FOR PRISON INMATES

When it comes to these fundamental conflicts, elected officials have to choose. And, time and time again, Ocasio-Cortez has sided with extreme gender ideology over common sense and biological reality. She may get away with it as a member of Congress representing a deep-blue district, or even if she runs for the Senate in New York. Yet if Ocasio-Cortez actually has presidential ambitions, her extreme record as a “girl’s girl” will surely come back to haunt her.
Just ask Kamala Harris.
Brad Polumbo is an independent journalist and host of the Brad vs Everyone podcast.

articles.headline: Cook County and Connecticut urge Supreme Court to uphold bans on ‘exceptionally dangerous’ AR-15s
keyFacts: Cook County and Connecticut urged the Supreme Court to uphold their bans on purchasing AR-15 and similar semiautomatic rifles.
Pro-gun groups and the Trump administration argued the bans are unconstitutional, saying the Second Amendment protects popular firearms.
The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on December 2 and is expected to rule by the end of June.
body: The Supreme Court will hear a pair of cases over the legality of sweeping “assault weapons” bans later this year, and the local governments at the center of the lawsuits are urging the high court this week to let them ban the firearms they claim are responsible for the “most tragic and frightening crimes.”

The high court will hear the consolidated cases Viramontes v. Cook County and Grant v. Higgins , challenging the “assault weapons” bans in Cook County, Illinois, and Connecticut, respectively, in December. The bans at the center of the consolidated case outlaw the purchase of AR-15 and similar semiautomatic rifles, with the justices set to rule on whether those bans violate the Second or 14th amendments. Both local governments filed their briefs to the Supreme Court this week, emphasizing their arguments that the bans are lawful because the AR-15 and similar weapons are not ordinary firearms.

“The Framers did not intend to permit the possession or use of ‘any weapon whatsoever in any manner whatsoever and for whatever purpose,'” Cook County State’s Attorney Eileen O’Neill Burke said in the county’s brief to the high court. “This principle is deeply rooted in our Nation’s history, which is replete with common-sense regulations of weapons that are exceptionally dangerous, lethal, and prone to misuse.”

“When weapons are introduced into society that have the capability to perpetrate some of our most tragic and frightening crimes, from mass shootings to assassination attempts, democratically elected legislators are permitted to respond with appropriate regulation,” O’Neill Burke added, later pointing to the fact that an AR-15 was used in the July 2024 assassination attempt against President Donald Trump.

The Cook County brief also emphasized the AR-15’s “military features,” as part of the argument that the firearms covered under the ban are “offensive weapons of war designed for maximum lethality and are not customarily used for self-defense,” and therefore not protected under the Second Amendment.
There are as many as 30 million AR-15s and similar rifles in circulation in the U.S., according to the National Shooting Sports Foundation .

Elizabeth Prelogar, a lawyer representing Connecticut officials and former U.S. solicitor general under the Biden administration, wrote for the state’s brief that the weapons covered under the ban are “distinctively capable of swiftly inflicting fatal injuries on a scale similar to its military counterpart, the M-16.” Prelogar also mentioned various infamous mass shootings during which the AR-15 was used by gunmen, opening with discussing the 2012 Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting, which killed 20 students and six school faculty.

“That capacity for lethality comes from a mix of features that permit even an unskilled gunman to rapidly fire high-velocity bullets that leave catastrophic wounds. Tragically, real-world experience confirms the AR-15’s singular dangerousness: From Sandy Hook to Las Vegas to Parkland to Uvalde, shooters have used the AR-15 or similar weapons in the vast majority of mass-casualty shootings this century,” Prelogar wrote for the state’s brief.
“The Constitution does not prevent Connecticut from banning the very weapons that have wrought incalculable harm and unimaginable loss on the people of that State,” Prelogar added later in the brief.

The pro-gun groups suing over the pair of “assault weapons” bans have argued in their briefs that the AR-15, which is the most popular firearm in the country, has to be covered under the Second Amendment’s right to bear arms, otherwise local governments would find ways to enact sweeping bans on other types of guns.

“This is the next ‘great white whale’ of the gun advocacy space, so it doesn’t get much bigger,” Bill Sack, senior director of legal operations at the Second Amendment Foundation, previously told the Washington Examiner . “What is at stake is whether the Second Amendment protects the most popular firearms in the country.”
‘ASSAULT WEAPONS’ BANS ARE ON THEIR WAY TO THE SUPREME COURT

The Trump administration has sided with the pro-gun groups in the case, with Solicitor General D. John Sauer filing a brief last month arguing the pair of bans is unconstitutional and does not comport with the country’s history and tradition of firearms regulation.
The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments in the consolidated cases Viramontes v. Cook County and Grant v. Higgins on Dec. 2, with a ruling in the cases expected by the end of June.

articles.headline: It's our new daily game fixation and we all stink at it: Can you guess how much used cars cost?
keyFacts: PC Gamer published a review of a new daily browser game called The Daily Lowball, where players guess used car prices.
Players evaluate five real cars daily, receiving grades from A to F from a virtual boss and risking their streak if they fail.
PC Gamer staff reported struggling with the puzzle's difficulty, noting that poor guesses can result in being fired within the game.
body: I'm always on the lookout for a new daily game I can play on my phone because, quite honestly, I'll do just about anything to delay getting out of bed for just a few more minutes in the morning. If you're into games like Wordle but are looking for an interesting new twist, here's a pitch:
Wordle, but it's about pricing used cars

Congratulations on your new job at The Daily Lowball, a used car lot where you have to prove to your boss that you know how much second-hand vehicles are worth. Each day in the puzzle, you're served up five real cars complete with photos and stats: the make and model, what year it's from, how many miles it's got on it, and how much it sold for when it was new.

Then you enter a guess how much you think each used car was sold for on the date shown. You're graded from A-F on your guesses by your virtual boss, and if you want to keep your daily streak intact, you'd better be accurate. Perform poorly enough on any given day, or string a few bad days together, and you're fired—you'll have to start your streak over.

It's an easy game to grasp but boy, we here at PC Gamer sure stink at it. My first day on the lot wasn't so smooth after I completely misjudged the resale price of a 2014 Audi Allroad Quattro and utterly biffed my guess on a cherry red 2005 Dodge Neon SRT-4. I did a little better on the 2008 Mercury Grand Marquis and the 2001 Porsche Boxter, and actually nailed the 2001 GMC Yukon. That gave me a C average for the day, so at least my streak has begun.

The other members of PC Gamer I sent the puzzle to didn't fare that well, either. I won't name and shame but there were two Ds and one F among my coworkers. If I'm the lone car guy at PCG, we're all in trouble.

Turns out it's fun to peer at used cars and try to figure out what they're worth, or at least what some real-world person thought they were worth when they bought them. And questions abound while I played a few more past puzzles, like "How does someone only have 8,000 miles on their 1985 Mazda RX-7? What, do they live in a walkable city or something? Insanity."
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The site has a few other daily car-based games, like "Steal or Bad Deal" where you judge whether someone paid an acceptable amount for a used car or got ripped off, "Higher or Lower" where you're presented with two cars and have to guess which is more expensive, and a licence plate slot machine game where you try to roll a rare plate every day. Check out The Daily Lowball for yourself, and feel free to share your results in the comments.

Chris started playing PC games in the 1980s, started writing about them in the early 2000s, and (finally) started getting paid to write about them in the late 2000s. Following a few years as a regular freelancer, PC Gamer hired him in 2014, probably so he'd stop emailing them asking for more work. Chris has a love-hate relationship with survival games and an unhealthy fascination with the inner lives of NPCs. He's also a fan of offbeat simulation games, mods, and ignoring storylines in RPGs so he can make up his own.

articles.headline: Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s First DLC Is Out Now, Honors A Real Soldier Who Sustained Gruesome Injuries
keyFacts: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 released its first day-one DLC pack, the Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack, on October 23.
The $20 DLC pack adds real-life Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter as a playable character.
Proceeds from the DLC bundle will go to Activision's charity that helps military veterans find new jobs.
body: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 released today, October 23, and the game's first DLC pack is available now. In keeping with Call of Duty tradition, the day-one DLC is a Call of Duty Endowment (CODE) pack , with proceeds going to Activision's charity that supports military veterans find new jobs after they leave the service.
The CODE Valor Pack adds the real-life Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter to the game as a playable character.

Carpenter was in Marjah, Afghanistan, when, on November 21, 2010, he put himself in front of a grenade to help save the life of his fellow Marine, Nick Eufrazio. Carpenter sustained serious injuries from the grenade blast. He was unconscious for five weeks, had his teeth stripped from his mouth, and lost an eye. He sustained numerous other life-threatening injuries in the blast.

Carpenter received the Medal of Honor from President Barack Obama in 2014. At the ceremony, Obama said, "They found Kyle lying face down, directly over the blast area. His helmet was riddled with holes. His gear was melted. Part of his Kevlar vest was blown away. One of the doctors who treated him later said Kyle was, 'Literally wounded from the top of his head to his feet.'"

Carpenter underwent brain surgery to remove shrapnel from his head. He had about 40 other surgeries to addresses his injuries, which included a collapsed lung, fractured fingers, and one arm that broke in more than 30 places. He had multiple skin grafts and now has a prosthetic eye, a new jaw, and new teeth.

articles.headline: Abandoned Popcorn Time apps had to be disabled to prevent a zombie army
keyFacts: Eye Security researchers disabled a vulnerable updater in an abandoned Popcorn Time app to prevent malicious actors from creating a botnet.
Researchers said the insecure updater ran on millions of devices, allowing attackers to run software with full privileges.
Eye Security sent over two million disabling updates before transferring the domains to the Shadowserver Foundation.
body: Remember Popcorn Time, the app that served as an easy-to-use front end for streaming torrents of movies and TV shows? Development of the MPAA’s least-favorite app of the 2010s has been abandoned for years, but the “Netflix of Piracy” software is still installed on millions of devices that are just waiting to join a bot army. Researchers at Eye Security found the updater for a Popcorn Time fork called “Time4Popcorn” still running on tons of Windows, macOS, and Android devices located around the world, phoning home to now-abandoned web domains over unencrypted HTTP and running an outdated, insecure version of Chrome.
Abandoned Popcorn Time apps had to be disabled to prevent a zombie army
What old and vulnerable software might be running on your PC right now?

Eye Security’s Niels Teusink says the updater could have been used to install and run basically any kind of software with full privileges, easily enabling someone to create a botnet just by taking over one of the domains, using a man-in-the-middle attack to target specific devices, or perform surveillance by identifying the machines running the software.

Their solution was to register one of the domains and use it to send their own update that instructed the updater to disable itself. Despite ethical concerns about the fix, the researchers say their only alternative “was to do nothing,” pointing out, “The update process wasn’t doing anything functional anyway, it was only creating risk for users.”

Eye Security said on Windows devices, their update “simply stops and disables the service via the Service Control Manager” without deleting any files or anything else. On macOS, it uses a shell script to execute a command that blocks the update process from starting. They didn’t address the software on Android devices, where installing the update would still require actual user interaction first.

They had to tweak their update after it was uploaded to VirusTotal, causing security programs to flag it as malware and block it while leaving the vulnerable updater running. It’s unclear exactly how many devices were at risk, but Eye Security says it “sent out over 2 million update downloads” by March, when they stopped sending the update and transferred the domains they used to the Shadowserver Foundation, a web security non-profit.

ILHAN OMAR HIT WITH EXPULSION THREAT AS GOP LAWMAKER VOWS TO BOOT HER FROM CONGRESS OVER DOJ PROBE
Omar then turned her fire on Vice President JD Vance, adding, "Maybe you should focus on what your VP's real name is."

The verbal pushback came as Trump called on Omar to resign from Congress Thursday after Fox News Digital reported that Omar's birth name is Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, according to two people familiar with the ongoing federal investigation, including a law enforcement source.

ILHAN OMAR'S TURBULENT WEEK EXPLAINED: THE DUELING PROBES THAT THREW THE SOMALI-BORN PROGRESSIVE INTO CHAOS

When asked during an MS NOW interview this week whether there was any familial relationship with Elmi, Omar responded, "Not to my knowledge." Her spokesperson later said the answer was sarcastic and reiterated that Omar "repeatedly and unequivocally" denied the allegation.

articles.headline: Leclerc tops first USA practice as upgraded Ferrari shows early promise
keyFacts: Charles Leclerc set the fastest time in the first practice session at the United States Grand Prix using an upgraded Ferrari.
Ferrari, Red Bull, and McLaren introduced car updates for the opening session at the Circuit of the Americas.

body: United States GP: Charles Leclerc fastest in upgraded Ferrari in first practice in Austin as Mercedes rivals introduce updates

Ferrari, Red Bull, McLaren and Mercedes separated by narrow margins around COTA in Practice One; Antonelli in sixth on weekend he could clinch world title; watch second practice later on Friday at 10pm live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at the same time on Saturday
Friday 23 October 2026 20:20, UK
Charles Leclerc showed early promise in an upgraded Ferrari car to pip Red Bull's in-form Max Verstappen to the fastest time of first practice at the United States Grand Prix.

Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull all introduced fresh revisions to their cars for the opening hour of running at the Circuit of the Americas, which is staging the first leg of the sport's second of three end-of-season triple headers.

Ferrari's package features changes to their car's floor, sidepod and diffuser and showed speed on both the medium and soft tyres around the undulating COTA lap, with Leclerc ultimately setting the session's pace on the latter with a best lap of 1:36.052.

Verstappen, the winner of the last two races, finished 0.084s behind Leclerc although lost a quicker lap on the softs which was two tenths faster than the Ferrari due to a track limits violation at Turn 19.

Lando Norris was third in a McLaren car which also features changes as they bid to return to form after a difficult run of races saw them slip into the clutches of Red Bull in the Constructors' Championship battle for third.

World championship leaders Mercedes do not have fresh upgrades in Austin. But both of their drivers are back to running the package first introduced two races ago in Malaysia after George Russell reverted to the older-spec last time out in Singapore.

Russell finished fourth, 0.326s behind, in opening practice with title-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli fifth on a weekend the Italian could clinch 2026's world title if he wins on Sunday and his team-mate and Lewis Hamilton do not score sufficient points to stay in mathematical contention.
Hamilton was only sixth fastest in Friday's first session, half a second away from team-mate Leclerc, after his soft-tyre run did not come together. Oscar Piastri was seventh in the second McLaren.
Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle said: "It does look so close at the front.
"McLaren look in there too, Mercedes found some time. Ferrari you'd have to say just had an ounce of an advantage but it is early doors."

Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto was the top midfield runner with the eighth-fastest time although he faces a back-of-the-grid start in Sunday's race after taking two engine elements beyond the season's penalty-free allowance.

Arvid Lindblad was ninth for Racing Bulls in a session the team introduced a sixth internal combustion engine into his car, triggering a five-place grid penalty for the race. Liam Lawson was 10th quickest in the second Racing Bulls.

Williams finished 19th with Carlos Sainz and 22nd with Alex Albon, who did not set a lap time, as the team opted to spend the session running an aerodynamic testing programme to aid car development for this and next year.

articles.headline: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
keyFacts: Russia is intensifying attacks on Kyiv, targeting residential buildings and infrastructure as subway stations serve as makeshift shelters.
Kyiv's military administration reported 140 people were killed in the first eight months of 2026, marking a deadlier trend.
Strikes on energy infrastructure leave it unclear how Kyiv will supply heat, electricity, and water during the upcoming winter.
body: Until a few months ago, life was relatively peaceful in Kyiv when compared with the situation near the war's front lines elsewhere in Ukraine. Now, as Russia expands its attacks on the capital, Kyiv has increasingly become a front-line city.

With too few shelters for the 4 million residents of Kyiv, subway stations double as makeshift dormitories. Starting at about 10 every night, people create sleeping areas with mattresses and small tents. Children snuggle up to adults; pets seek comfort from their owners or find a spot among strangers between the cold walls.

"We're alive," Halyna told DW, holding her 5-year-old son, Roman, close. "We've been lucky once again." Most evenings — even when no air-raid siren has sounded — she takes the boy to the nearest subway station. Her apartment is located in the Lukyanivka district, which Russia has systematically targeted over the war's four years and eight months.
'These sick monsters don't care who they kill'

In September, 14-year-old Daniel Umanskyj was doing homework in his room when a Russian drone struck the apartment building in the central district of Pechersk. A neighbor named Vlad happened to be in the hallway with his daughter at the time of the strike. "We were late that day — and this saved our lives," Vlad said. "Daniel's death is a tragedy." He added: "These sick monsters don't care who they kill." Flowers have been planted in front of the damaged apartment building in memory of Daniel.
Russia also targets places where children gather. In early October, a drone struck a school building in southwestern Kyiv. Fortunately, pupils and teachers were already in shelters at the time.

"We've been teaching all the pupils in person because we have a large shelter that can accommodate more than 500 students," Valentyna Chorna, the school's principal, told DW. As there is enough space in the shelter for everyone, students in the first through ninth grades are able to go to school, she said.
Danger at home, at school — everywhere

Whether classes take place depends not only on the decision of the parents and the school administration: It also depends on whether shelters are available and how long the air-raid siren continues to sound. If an alarm sounds in the morning while children are still at home, they may not be able to go to school that day.
"This is an enormous burden for parents," said a colleague from the DW bureau in Kyiv, whose daughter attends school. "You have to go to work — and the child stays home alone."

"Even the walk to school is dangerous because an air-raid alarm can go off at any time," she said. Her daughter attends a school not far from the Antonov aircraft factory. "One day she texted me: ‘You can't imagine what a huge explosion that was!'" she said. "I don't know if something was shot down or if there was a strike somewhere." She added: "Things like that really scare children." And staying home brings its own risks.

In September, a Russian drone struck their building. The apartment itself wasn't damaged, and her daughter was at school that morning, but it was another reminder of just how much survival has become a matter of luck. When an air-raid siren sounds, no one knows who will be spared, she said.
Kyiv's population persists

Russia's attacks have become deadlier in 2026. According to the military administration in Kyiv, 140 people were killed in the capital during the first eight months of the year, compared with 172 for all of 2025. If this trend continues, 2026 could become Kyiv's deadliest year since the start of the Russian invasion in 2022.

Attacks on warehouses have led to shortages in supermarkets on a scale not seen since the early months of the war. At the end of September, emergency power outages resumed in Kyiv. The subway was paralyzed by a Russian attack. Given the strikes on the energy infrastructure, it is unclear how the capital can reliably supply residents with heat, electricity and water during the upcoming winter.

Despite Russia's attempts to render Kyiv uninhabitable, 72% of the city's residents said in September that they are prepared to endure the war for as long as necessary, the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology reported in early October. The authorities are striving to maintain normal life in the city, where the curfew has been shortened and now runs from 1 a.m. to 5 a.m.

Some facilities have even been allowed to continue operating during "yellow" alerts. During "red" alerts, however, people must immediately seek shelter: This could mean ballistic missiles, cruise missiles or massive combined attacks.
This article was originally written in Ukrainian.

articles.headline: Ahead of GTA 6, PlayStation 5 Sales Were Up 22%, Likely Due To Wolverine
keyFacts: PlayStation 5 sales increased by 22 percent, according to a Bloomberg report utilizing Circana data.
Circana Senior Director Mat Piscatella stated that the hardware boost was primarily driven by Marvel's Wolverine.
Piscatella noted that the Xbox Series did not experience a similar sales increase during the same month.
body: The latter part of 2026 has been packed with excellent games, all leading up to GTA 6 on November 19, so it's not surprising that PS5 sales have jumped over last month.

PlayStation 5 sales have jumped by 22%, according to a report from Bloomberg, with data from Circana. And, while it's likely that the buildup to GTA 6 has contributed to those sales, it looks like it was September's all-star lineup of games, and particularly Marvel's Wolverine, that were primarily behind the PS5's recent success.

We reached out to Circana Senior Director and Video Game Industry Advisor Mat Piscatella for comment on these recent sales increases, and he told us that despite its middling reception, Wolverine drove quite a bit of hardware sales. "PS5's hardware boost was primarily driven by Marvel's Wolverine. NBA 2K27 and Grand Theft Auto VI also likely helped," he said. However, he added that "Xbox Series did not get a similar sales boost during the month."

When IGN reviewed Wolverine, we gave it a middling 6 out of 10, with reviewer Simon Cardy saying, "Marvel's Wolverine's slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion, so much so that even its strong character work can't quite save it from being anything more than okay."

In the weeks that have followed the game's release, the community has also been mixed on the game, and Insomniac has had to respond by fixing some of the more hand-holdy mechanics, like adding a toggle for the ever-present scent trail that guides you to objectives . But, even early on, there were signs that Wolverine was selling .

Now, more than a month after release, Wolverine seems like it was absolutely a success, with Piscatella saying, "For Marvel's Wolverine, [it's] tough to give things a vibe check without understanding folks' frame of reference, but it was the month's best-seller, ranks 11th year-to-date, with a hardware bundle that seems to have sold out and the market's best-selling accessory during the month with the limited edition Marvel's Wolverine DualSense. Seems pretty good to me. But, we'll have to see how the legs are over time. It wasn't as big as say Marvel's Spider-Man 2, but I don't think that would have ever been a reasonable assumption."
That hardware bundle was likely a big reason why PlayStation's sales were so rosy over the last month. The controller looked amazing, and started selling out before the game even launched.

Looking ahead to GTA 6, though, if a game like Wolverine was able to drive hardware like this, I can only imagine that GTA is going to make an even bigger impact. We've already started to see signs of that happening, too. Just a couple of weeks ago, the PS5 Pro started selling out enough that used models started going for as much as $1,400, $500 more than their shelf price. And, to this day, that price still holds, with the PS5 Pro available on both Amazon and Gamestop for $1,399.

At that price, it's going to be interesting to see sales data for this coming month, and how many people are willing to fork over that kind of cash for a new console. After all, there have been rumors this week that the next-generation Xbox Project Helix may cost up to $1,800 . There were also leaks that suggest that for the PS6, just the RAM and SSD alone will cost around $680 , which could see Sony's next-gen console commanding a similar price.
